# core-math-java test vectors: hypot, binary64.
# upstream: https://gitlab.inria.fr/core-math/core-math
# source:   src/binary64/hypot/hypot.c (cr_hypot)
# commit:   0ce0cbc15935e24c656280e5a46c34e89f301b7a
# reference build: gcc 13.2.0, -O2 -ffp-contract=off -mfma (see tools/cmref/build.sh)
# columns:  y x result
#
# Written by tools/mkvectors.py; every result is the bits the
# C entry point returns for that input.
#
# directed: the values of AGENTS.md 5.1, both sides of every
# comparison threshold of the translation, and the exceptional
# entries the entry point can reach.
# thresholds: the exact triples, the subnormal pairs, the special values in either
#   position, the 2^-52 ratio bounds, and the 16 rows of the near-midpoint family X^2 +
#   Y^2 = Z^2 + 1 of the core-math-quality hypot candidate in both argument orders
# double rounding: no scan.  --frontier walks the whole binary32 domain of a
#   one-argument function, and a two-argument function has 2^64 argument pairs, so the
#   directed grid and the random sweep stand in for it
# worst cases: every 33th of the 33174 rows of hypot.wc
# random: xorshift64 from seed 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15, 2 draws per case, 1000 cases, in the
#   order they were drawn
#--- directed
